import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Ben Green's Open Problem 54

*References:*

- [Ben Green's Open Problem 54](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.54)
- Original formulation: M. Talagrand, *Are All Sets of Positive Measure Essentially Convex?*, in Operator Theory:
Advances and Applications, 77, 1995 Birkhäuser Verlag Basel/Switzerland.
-/

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped Pointwise ENNReal

namespace Green54

/-- The infinite-dimensional Gaussian measure γ∞ on ℝ^ℕ,
defined as the countable product of standard Gaussian measures. -/
noncomputable def gaussianMeasureInf : Measure (ℕ → ℝ) :=
  Measure.infinitePi (fun _ : ℕ => gaussianReal 0 1)

/--
Let $K \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a balanced compact set (that is, $\lambda K \subseteq K$ whenever
$|\lambda| \leq 1$) and suppose that the normalised Gaussian measure $\gamma_n(K) \geq 0.99$.
Does $10K$ contain a compact convex set $C$ with $\gamma_n(C) \geq 0.01$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 46 52 60]
theorem green_54 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ K : Set (ℕ → ℝ), IsCompact K → Balanced ℝ K → (0.99 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤
    gaussianMeasureInf K → ∃ C : Set (ℕ → ℝ), IsCompact C ∧ Convex ℝ C ∧ C ⊆ (10 : ℝ) • K ∧
    (0.01 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ gaussianMeasureInf C := by
  sorry

/--
The same statement is known to be false for 2K instead of 10K.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 46 52 60]
theorem green_54_known_case : ¬ (∀ K : Set (ℕ → ℝ), IsCompact K → Balanced ℝ K → (0.99 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤
    gaussianMeasureInf K → ∃ C : Set (ℕ → ℝ), IsCompact C ∧ Convex ℝ C ∧ C ⊆ (2 : ℝ) • K ∧
    (0.01 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ gaussianMeasureInf C) := by
  sorry

end Green54

findings.description: The containment at line 47, `C ⊆ (10 : ℝ) • K`, uses real scalar dilation: `{10 * x | x ∈ K}`. The source's `10K` is the tenfold Minkowski sum, allowing ten independently chosen elements of K. Balancedness does not imply convexity and does not identify these operations. This changes the bounded-sum problem into a substantially stronger, elementary-false dilation question. In Lean, I verified that a compact balanced union of two coordinate segments has a point in its tenfold Minkowski sum that belongs to no real dilation of the set. A counterexample satisfying the Gaussian-measure hypothesis is described in the notes.
findings.source_evidence: Talagrand, Are All Sets of Positive Measure Essentially Convex? (1995), p. 296, explicitly defines `S_n(K) = {∑_{i≤n} x_i : x_i ∈ K}` and states Problem 2.3 using S_n(K): https://page-one.springer.com/pdf/preview/10.1007/978-3-0348-9090-8_25 . Green's Problem 54 uses `10K` in this sumset sense, consistently with Problems 50–53: https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.54 . Hua–Song–Tudose, arXiv:2605.10908v2, §1, also explicitly cites Green's Problem 54 and writes the operation as a repeated Minkowski sum.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `C ⊆ (10 : ℝ) • K` with `C ⊆ (10 : ℕ) • K`. With the existing Pointwise scope, this is the tenfold Minkowski sum; I checked in Lean that it equals `∑ _ : Fin 10, K`. Handle the updated answer/category separately as described in status_issues.

findings.description: The containment at line 56 uses `(2 : ℝ) • K = {2 * x | x ∈ K}`, rather than `K + K`. Consequently, the negated universal statement only asserts a counterexample to finding a large convex subset in a dilation. The source's known case asserts a counterexample even after adding two independently chosen points of K. Since real dilation by 2 is contained in K + K, failure for the dilation is a weaker conclusion and does not state the cited two-sum obstruction.
findings.source_evidence: Green's comments to Problem 54 say that the answer is no with `2K` instead of `10K`: https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.54 . Talagrand's current My favorite problems, §2, defines the operation as `A + ··· + A (n times)` and states that n = 2 fails, even for an additional dilation `L(A + A)`: https://michel.talagrand.net/Korea15.pdf . Hua–Song–Tudose, arXiv:2605.10908v2, §1, attributes this two-Minkowski-sum obstruction to Talagrand (1995), Proposition 2.6.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `C ⊆ (2 : ℝ) • K` with `C ⊆ K + K`, or equivalently `C ⊆ (2 : ℕ) • K`. Keep the outer negation and the solved category.

status_issues.source_status: The intended Minkowski-sum problem has a positive solution. Hua, Song, and Tudose announced the solution on 11 May 2026; their v2 of 10 July 2026 supplies explicit constants sufficient for Green's stated tenfold-sum question.
status_issues.evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10908 and its v2 source, Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 5.2. The latter gives a convex body of Gaussian measure at least c inside b⁻¹(A+A+A), provided γ_n(A)>5/6 and 2b+c≤1. Taking b=1/3 and c=1/4 gives a subset of the ninefold Minkowski sum. For nonempty balanced K, zero belongs to K, so this lies in the tenfold sum. A compactness argument using finite-coordinate projections extends this uniform result to Green's compact countable-product setting. Talagrand's current https://michel.talagrand.net/Korea15.pdf also records the breakthrough.
status_issues.suggested_change: After fixing the Minkowski-sum operation, change the category to `research solved`, replace `answer(sorry)` with `answer(True)`, and cite Hua–Song–Tudose (2026), including the specialization of constants.

sources_consulted: https://page-one.springer.com/pdf/preview/10.1007/978-3-0348-9090-8_25 — Talagrand (1995), pp. 295–296, including the definition of S_n and Problem 2.3
https://michel.talagrand.net/Korea15.pdf — My favorite problems, current July 2026 version, §2 and references
https://arxiv.org/e-print/2605.10908 — Hua–Song–Tudose, On Talagrand's Convexity Conjecture, v2, introduction and §5
https://arxiv.org/e-print/2502.10382 — Johnston, On creating convexity in high dimensions, introduction, quotation of Talagrand (2010), and updated status discussion

review.notes:
All three declarations were checked. `gaussianMeasureInf` faithfully matches the product of standard normal measures specified on p. 296 of Talagrand's original paper. The infinite-dimensional domain matches Green's source, notwithstanding the finite-dimensional notation in the theorem's docstring. Lean checks established normalization, Gaussian marginals, measurability of compact sets, the exact decimal constants, zero measure of singletons, and existence of compact balanced sets with measure at least 0.99. `/workspace/review/validation.lean` and `/workspace/review/cross.lean` compile without errors or warnings.

A genuine high-measure counterexample to the dilation question: in R^7 take A = {x : ||x|| ≤ R and |x_i| ≥ δ||x|| for every i}. Choose R large and δ>0 small so that γ_7(A)>0.995. A is compact and balanced, and each coordinate hyperplane meets any dilation of A only at zero. Every convex subset of such a dilation therefore lies in one orthant or in a line, giving Gaussian measure at most 2⁻⁷=1/128<0.01. Multiply A by a compact balanced Gaussian tail box of measure >0.995. The resulting K in R^N has measure >0.99; projection to its first seven coordinates proves that no dilation of K contains a convex subset of measure 0.01.

For the status extension to infinite dimension, let S be the ninefold sum of K. Apply the finite-dimensional result to each projection, obtaining convex C_m ⊆ p_m(S) of measure ≥1/4. The compact sets S ∩ p_m⁻¹(C_m) have measure ≥0.24. A Hausdorff-convergent subsequence has a compact limit of measure ≥0.24, and convexity of the increasingly long coordinate projections makes that limit convex. Details are recorded in `/workspace/review/mathematical-checks.md`.

The original chapter's first two pages were accessible and contain the relevant definition and problem; the full chapter and the 2010 ACM article were access-restricted. The original excerpt and the author's later explicit restatement suffice to settle the declarations.

submission.summary: Replaced the real dilations with the tenfold Minkowski sum `(10 : ℕ) • K` and the twofold sum `K + K`. Updated the docstrings to specify Minkowski sums and the countable Gaussian product. Also recorded the verified positive solution with `answer(True)`, a solved category, and the Hua–Song–Tudose reference. The required compile command succeeds with only the expected `sorry` warnings.

/-!

- Original formulation: M. Talagrand, *Are All Sets of Positive Measure Essentially Convex?*, in Operator Theory:

- [HST26] D. Hua, A. Song, and S. Tudose, *On Talagrand's Convexity Conjecture*,

open scoped Pointwise ENNReal

namespace Green54

/-- The infinite-dimensional Gaussian measure γ∞ on ℝ^ℕ,

noncomputable def gaussianMeasureInf : Measure (ℕ → ℝ) :=

/--

convex set $C$ with $\gamma_\infty(C) \geq 0.01$?

The answer is yes by [HST26, Corollary 5.2], taking $b=1/3$ and $c=1/4$ and passing from
finite-dimensional projections to the compact infinite-dimensional setting.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 46 52 60]
theorem green_54 :
    answer(True) ↔ ∀ K : Set (ℕ → ℝ), IsCompact K → Balanced ℝ K → (0.99 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤
    gaussianMeasureInf K → ∃ C : Set (ℕ → ℝ), IsCompact C ∧ Convex ℝ C ∧ C ⊆ (10 : ℕ) • K ∧
    (0.01 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ gaussianMeasureInf C := by
  sorry

/--
The same statement is known to be false for the twofold Minkowski sum $K + K$ instead of the
tenfold Minkowski sum.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 46 52 60]
theorem green_54_known_case : ¬ (∀ K : Set (ℕ → ℝ), IsCompact K → Balanced ℝ K → (0.99 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤
    gaussianMeasureInf K → ∃ C : Set (ℕ → ℝ), IsCompact C ∧ Convex ℝ C ∧ C ⊆ K + K ∧
    (0.01 : ℝ≥0∞) ≤ gaussianMeasureInf C) := by
  sorry

end Green54
